correction.text: Lu as drawn, without the lands that were Ju's (Chu from 431) and Tan's (Yue from 414)

keyframe_review.note: 43,571 km2 for 750-481, bbox 115.0-120.7 E, 34.7-36.5 N, which runs from Shandong's centre to the southeast coast; the Lu page says its territory 'mainly covered the central and southwest regions of what is now Shandong Province'. The states table of the Spring and Autumn period page lists Ju as a separate state until 431 ('to Chu') and Tan (郯) until 414 ('to Yue'), and Cliopatria hands exactly those cells (36 to Chu, 18 to Yue) out of Lu's shape in 404. They are removed here for the whole life of the shape: reading by overlap, confidence 2. The 130 cells that go to Qi in 404 are kept as Lu's (the Warring States page: Lu 'was occupied by Qi'). The page has no area figure.

keyframe_review.note: 38,794 km2 for 480-451: the shape loses 24 cells on the west (115.0-115.9 E, 35.5-36.2 N) to Song in Cliopatria (page silent; the states table has Cao 'to Song' in 487 but no Lu land). Same correction as the 750 shape.

keyframe_review.note: 39,169 km2 for 450-405 (3 cells more than 480, from Zhu and Xu; page silent). Same correction as the 750 shape: Ju fell to Chu in 431 and Tan to Yue in 414 (states table), so the shape that keeps them in Lu until 405 overstates Lu.

8,948 km2 for 404-285 (115.65-117.07 E, 35.3-36.4 N): central and southwest Shandong round Qufu, matching 'its territory mainly covered the central and southwest regions of what is now Shandong Province'. The loss from the 450 shape (185 cells: 130 to Qi, 36 to Chu, 18 to Yue) is explained in the ledger. The page has no area to compare.

4,135 km2 for 284-257: Cliopatria drops 34 cells (115.8-117.0 E, 35.6-36.3 N) to Qi. The Warring States page says only that 'Smaller states like Lu would quickly fall under the power of bigger states' and, in a parenthesis, 'Lu was occupied by Qi' (undated); the year is the shape's (confidence 1 in the ledger).

4,135 km2 for 256-248, identical to the 284 shape. Chu annexed Lu in 249 on the Lu page ('In 249 BC King Kaolie of the state of Chu invaded and annexed Lu'); the states table of the Spring and Autumn period page says 256 BCE. The shape stands to 249 (Cliopatria runs one year longer).

notes: Wikidata Q555994 is shared with 'aq-qoyunlu' (Aq Qoyunlu, 1407-1511, Anatolia and Iran): a different state; this dossier covers only the Cliopatria Name 'Lu'. Lu's own annexations in the Spring and Autumn period states table (Ji 721, Xuqu 620, Zhuan 585, Yu 524, Lan 521 'to Lu') have no location on any page opened, so they are not ledger events (a region could only be guessed); the Cliopatria shape does not change across them. A gap-filler could open the pages of those small states. The 562 division of Lu's army among the Three Huan families (states table text) and the exile of Duke Zhao are internal, undated or not territorial, and are not events. Disagreements: end of Lu 249 (Lu page) vs 256 (states table); the Warring States page's 'Lu was occupied by Qi' has no date, so the 404 and 284 Qi events are Cliopatria's years at confidence 1. The correction removing the Ju and Tan lands from the pre-404 shapes rests on a reading of the states table and on overlap with Chu's and Yue's 404 shapes; the Chu dossier (ea-01) dates Ju to 431 and puts its 404 shape north to 35.8 N. Region names: 'Qufu' is not in the gazetteer (coordinates 116.99 E, 35.58 N used) and is listed in gazetteer_names_needed. Counterparts without a Lu-side dossier: 'zhu' and 'song' are Cliopatria rows of group ea-01 (other parts); Ju (state) and Tan (state) need dossiers (they are not Cliopatria rows). Budget: 4 pages (up to 5).
